title: Node.js Reference
description: A compact reference for Node.js 24: CLI flags and npm commands, modules, the file system, events and streams, HTTP and Express 5, async helpers, node:test and node:sqlite, each linked to the lesson that explains it.

entries.name: node file.js
entries.summary: Runs a JavaScript file. Extra words after the file name become command-line arguments. node -p evaluates and prints an expression; node alone opens the REPL.

entries.name: node --watch
entries.summary: Restarts the program whenever a file it loaded changes. Stable since Node 22; use it in a dev script.

entries.name: node --env-file
entries.summary: Loads NAME=value lines from a file into process.env before the program starts. --env-file-if-exists ignores a missing file.
notes: Variables already set in the environment take precedence over the file.

entries.name: process.argv
entries.summary: Array of command-line arguments: the node binary, the script path, then user arguments as strings.

entries.name: process.env
entries.summary: Object holding the environment variables of the process. Every value is a string; unset names read as undefined.

entries.name: process.on('SIGTERM')
entries.summary: Registers a handler for an operating-system signal. SIGTERM is sent by supervisors before stopping a process; SIGINT is Ctrl+C. process.exit(code) ends the process.

entries.name: npm install
entries.summary: Installs a package into node_modules and records it in package.json and package-lock.json. Without a name, installs everything the project lists. npm init -y creates the package.json first.

example.code:
npm init -y
npm install express
npm install --save-dev prettier

entries.name: npm ci
entries.summary: Clean install of the exact versions in package-lock.json; fails if the lockfile and package.json disagree. Use on servers and in CI.

entries.name: npm run <script>
entries.summary: Runs a script from package.json with node_modules/.bin on the path. start and test can be run without the word run; npx runs a package's command directly.
entries.syntax: npm run dev | npm start | npm test | npx prettier --write .

entries.name: import / export
entries.summary: ES module syntax. Named exports are imported in braces by their exact name; the single default export can take any name.
entries.syntax: import name, { a, b as c } from './file.js';
notes: Relative paths must start with ./ or ../ and include the file extension.

entries.name: node: prefix
entries.summary: Marks a built-in module so it can never be shadowed by an npm package of the same name.

entries.name: "type": "module"
entries.summary: package.json field that makes .js files ES modules. Without it they are CommonJS; .mjs and .cjs extensions override the field.

entries.name: require / module.exports
entries.summary: CommonJS: module.exports defines what a file exposes and require() loads it synchronously. createRequire(import.meta.url) builds a require for use inside an ES module.

entries.name: import.meta.dirname / filename / url
entries.summary: Location of the current ES module: folder path, file path (Node 20.11+) and file:// URL. Replaces __dirname and __filename.

entries.name: import ... with { type: 'json' }
entries.summary: Imports a JSON file as a parsed object; the import attribute is required. For loading a module on demand, import() returns a promise.

entries.name: readFile()
entries.summary: Reads a whole file. Pass 'utf8' to get a string; without an encoding it resolves with a Buffer.

entries.name: writeFile() / appendFile()
entries.summary: writeFile creates or replaces a file with the given content; appendFile adds to the end.
entries.syntax:
await writeFile('todo.txt', 'Buy milk\n');
await appendFile('todo.txt', 'Call Ada\n');

entries.name: mkdir()
entries.summary: Creates a folder. With recursive: true it creates missing parents and ignores folders that already exist. rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true }) deletes a tree.

entries.name: readdir()
entries.summary: Lists the entries of a folder. With withFileTypes: true each entry has isFile() and isDirectory().
entries.syntax: const entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });

entries.name: stat()
entries.summary: Returns size, timestamps and type checks for a path; rejects with code ENOENT when it does not exist.
entries.syntax: const info = await stat(path); info.size; info.mtime;

entries.name: readFileSync() and friends
entries.summary: Blocking versions in node:fs (readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync). Fine at startup or in scripts, never inside request handlers.

entries.name: path.join() / path.resolve()
entries.summary: join concatenates segments with the platform separator; resolve turns a path into an absolute one using the working directory. basename and extname extract the file name and extension.

entries.name: EventEmitter
entries.summary: Base class for anything that emits events. on adds a listener, once adds a one-shot listener, off removes one and emit calls them synchronously in order.
notes: An 'error' event with no listener throws.
events.once(emitter, name) returns a promise for the next emission.

entries.name: createReadStream() / createWriteStream()
entries.summary: Readable and writable streams over files. The reader delivers chunks (64 KiB by default) that can be consumed with for await; the writer is typically the last stage of a pipeline.
entries.syntax: for await (const chunk of createReadStream(path, { encoding: 'utf8' })) { ... }

entries.name: readline.createInterface()
entries.summary: Turns any readable stream into an async iterable of lines; crlfDelay: Infinity treats CRLF as one line break.
entries.syntax: for await (const line of createInterface({ input, crlfDelay: Infinity })) { ... }

entries.name: pipeline()
entries.summary: Connects streams, handles backpressure, forwards errors, destroys every stream on failure and returns a promise (from node:stream/promises).

entries.name: Transform
entries.summary: A stream that changes data on the way through; implement transform(chunk, encoding, callback) and call callback(null, output). Readable.from(iterable) turns an array or generator into a stream.
entries.syntax: new Transform({ transform(chunk, enc, cb) { cb(null, modified); } })

entries.name: http.createServer()
entries.summary: Creates a server that calls your handler with (req, res) for every request; listen(port) starts accepting connections.

entries.name: req.method / req.url / req.headers
entries.summary: The incoming request: upper-case method, path plus query string, and an object of lower-cased headers. The body is read as a stream.

entries.name: res.writeHead() / res.end()
entries.summary: writeHead sets the status and headers; end sends the final chunk and finishes the response. Every request must be ended exactly once.

entries.name: fetch()
entries.summary: Built-in HTTP client with the browser API. Resolves for any status; check response.ok. Accepts a signal for timeouts.
entries.syntax: const response = await fetch(url, { method, headers, body, signal });

entries.name: express() / app.listen()
entries.summary: Creates an Express application and starts an HTTP server for it.

entries.name: app.get() / post() / put() / patch() / delete()
entries.summary: Register a handler for one HTTP method and path. Path segments starting with a colon become req.params; the query string becomes req.query.

entries.name: res.status() / res.json() / res.send()
entries.summary: status sets the code and chains; json sends JSON; send sends a string as HTML, a Buffer as binary or an object as JSON. All end the response.

entries.name: app.use() and middleware
entries.summary: Registers a (req, res, next) function that runs for every request (or every request under a prefix). Each middleware responds or calls next(). express.static(folder) is the built-in file server.

entries.name: express.json()
entries.summary: Middleware that parses JSON request bodies into req.body when Content-Type is application/json; limit 100 kB by default.

entries.name: express.Router()
entries.summary: A mini application with its own routes and middleware, mounted under a prefix with app.use.
entries.syntax: const router = Router(); router.get('/', handler); app.use('/api/books', router);

entries.name: Error-handling middleware
entries.summary: A middleware with four parameters (err, req, res, next), registered last. Express 5 also routes rejected promises from async handlers to it.
entries.syntax: app.use((err, req, res, next) => { res.status(err.status ?? 500).json({ error: '...' }); });

entries.name: util.promisify()
entries.summary: Wraps an error-first callback function so that it returns a promise.
entries.syntax: const run = promisify(exec); const { stdout } = await run('node --version');

entries.name: timers/promises setTimeout()
entries.summary: Promise-based timer: await it to pause an async function. Accepts a signal for cancellation.
entries.syntax: import { setTimeout as sleep } from 'node:timers/promises'; await sleep(500);

entries.name: Promise.all() / allSettled()
entries.summary: Run independent promises in parallel. all rejects on the first failure; allSettled waits for every result and reports each outcome.

entries.name: AbortSignal.timeout()
entries.summary: Creates a signal that aborts after a delay; pass it to fetch, timers or fs functions to enforce a deadline (rejects with TimeoutError).

entries.name: test() / describe() / it()
entries.summary: Define tests with node:test. describe groups tests, it (alias of test) defines one; async callbacks are awaited. Run them with node --test.

entries.name: beforeEach() / afterEach() / before() / after()
entries.summary: Hooks that run around each test or once per suite, for fresh fixtures and cleanup such as closing a server.

entries.name: node:assert/strict
entries.summary: Assertions with strict equality: equal, deepEqual, ok, throws, rejects, match.
entries.syntax: assert.equal(actual, expected); assert.deepEqual(obj, { id: 1 }); assert.throws(fn, TypeError);

entries.name: mock.fn() / mock.method()
entries.summary: Create a function that records its calls, or replace a method for the duration of a test; inspect callCount() and calls[i].arguments.

entries.name: new DatabaseSync(path)
entries.summary: Opens or creates an SQLite database file from node:sqlite; ':memory:' creates a temporary in-memory database. close() releases it.

entries.name: db.exec(sql)
entries.summary: Runs one or more SQL statements without parameters and returns nothing; used for schema setup and BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.
entries.syntax: db.exec('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL)');

entries.name: db.prepare(sql)
entries.summary: Compiles a statement with ? or $name placeholders and returns a StatementSync to execute with values.
entries.syntax: const insert = db.prepare('INSERT INTO books (title) VALUES (?)');

entries.name: statement.run() / get() / all()
entries.summary: run executes a write and returns { changes, lastInsertRowid }; get returns the first row or undefined; all returns every row as an array of objects.

example.code:
const { lastInsertRowid } = insert.run('Dune', 'Frank Herbert', 1965);
const book = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM books WHERE id = ?').get(lastInsertRowid);
